Exclude argument is not passed on to tar collecting data on units
It appears the exclude (-x / --exclude) was first developed for a specific set of juju specific files.

Since juju crashdump now also collects data from other places on the system, it would be useful to pass the exclude list on to the tar command collecting data elsewhere too.

https://github.com/juju/juju-crashdump/blob/2ec95c6a0e51dfae2410136652e01ed84d3a7fb1/jujucrashdump/crashdump.py#L270-L282

To address the issue, we need to modify the `crashdump.py` file to ensure that the exclude list is passed on to the tar command collecting data elsewhere. The issue points to lines 270-282 in the `crashdump.py` file. We should start by opening the file and navigating to those lines to understand the current implementation and plan our modifications. Let's open the `crashdump.py` file and navigate to line 270.
```
open jujucrashdump/crashdump.py 270
```

The issue suggests that we need to pass the exclude list on to the tar command collecting data elsewhere. We can see that the tar command is being constructed in lines 270-276, and the exclude list is not currently being passed on.

To fix this, we need to modify the tar command to include the exclude list. We can do this by adding a `--exclude` option to the tar command for each item in the exclude list. Let's make the necessary edits to the code to include this functionality. We will iterate through the exclude list and add a `--exclude` option for each item.
